headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: a writable, networked coding IDE can ingest and act on content from a non-runnable prompt-engineering repo via shared files/clipboard/MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing repository with no runnable safeguards; Agent B has clipboard, workspace files, and MCP inputs plus permissive tool use. That creates a plausible bridge where A-authored content can be copied or opened in B and treated as instructions. The pathway is documented by B’s surfaces and A’s content-writing role, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b or opened in agent_b workspace files
IF agent_b parses file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based prompt ingestion for agent_b
Keep agent_a outputs in a separate read-only folder
Add a manual provenance check before agent_b follows pasted instructions
Turn off MCP servers for sessions that process untrusted text
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads workspace files and has broad network egress, while Agent A is a content-writing repo that may contain arbitrary text artifacts. If A’s files are placed in B’s shared filesystem, B can ingest them and transmit contents to its model backend or external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are stored in agent_b's shared local filesystem
IF agent_b sends opened file contents to its inference backend or MCP-connected services
mitigations: Store agent_a artifacts outside agent_b workspace
Restrict agent_b network egress during review sessions
Use separate OS users for the two agents
Review and redact sensitive text before opening in agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via local filesystem across instances. Agent A is non-runnable and has no write controls, so the conflict is one-sided but still dangerous when A’s outputs are used to drive B’s edits. Because B’s defaults include mutable shared state and no locking is documented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF agent_b instances operate on the same local filesystem or git repo
IF agent_a-derived instructions are used to generate edits in agent_b without locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes git state
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Check for file locks before edits
requires-engineering: add concurrency locking around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s Cascade loop can act on tool outputs and modify files, while Agent A is a prompt-engineering content source that may be treated as authoritative guidance. If B consumes A’s text without verification, errors can cascade into code or repo changes. The interaction is inferred from B’s agentic editing defaults and A’s content-writing role.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as the basis for edits or commands
IF agent_b does not verify A-derived claims before acting
mitigations: Require a human review step before commits
Ask agent_b to cite source lines before acting
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for A-derived tasks
Compare A-derived claims against independent sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Agent A, and Agent B’s docs only show general workspace/code handling. The pair therefore presents only a weak compliance concern from shared handling of open files and model-provider keys, not a proven policy breach. I do not cite only one agent because the risk is pairwise but under-specified.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b workspace files
IF agent_b is used under a policy that forbids external model-provider transmission
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b sessions
Use a local-only policy for sensitive projects
Review retention settings before opening files
Separate compliance-sensitive workspaces
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
